content.text: /ext:medcp Which antidepressant classes are most commonly used in older adults (³65)?
I'll query the clinical records to see what antidepressants are prescribed to older adults. Let me first look at the available tables.

This is an OMOP CDM database. Antidepressants map through the ATC hierarchy (ATC class **N06A**). I'll use `drug_era` joined to the ATC subclasses (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, etc.) via `concept_ancestor`, restricted to patients ≥65 at drug start.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c_anc.concept_code AS atc_code,
       c_anc.concept_name AS antidepressant_class,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients,
       COUNT(*) AS n_drug_eras
FROM omop.drug_era de
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = de.person_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept c_anc ON c_anc.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
WHERE c_anc.vocabulary_id = 'ATC'
  AND c_anc.concept_class_id = 'ATC 4th'
  AND c_anc.concept_code LIKE 'N06A%'
  AND (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM de.drug_era_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
GROUP BY c_anc.concept_code, c_anc.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

The "Other antidepressants" (N06AX) group is the largest, but that ATC 4th-level bucket lumps together distinct classes (SNRIs, mirtazapine, bupropion, trazodone). Let me break it down to the ingredient level so the class picture is accurate.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT ing.concept_name AS ingredient,
       COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients
FROM omop.drug_era de
JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = de.person_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept cls ON cls.concept_id = ca.ancestor_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca2 ON ca2.descendant_concept_id = de.drug_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept ing ON ing.concept_id = ca2.ancestor_concept_id
WHERE cls.vocabulary_id = 'ATC'
  AND cls.concept_code = 'N06AX'
  AND ing.vocabulary_id = 'RxNorm'
  AND ing.concept_class_id = 'Ingredient'
  AND (YEAR(de.drug_era_start_date) - p.year_of_birth) >= 65
GROUP BY ing.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

Based on the EHR (OMOP CDM) data, restricted to patients aged ≥65 at the start of each antidepressant era:

## Antidepressant use in older adults (≥65)

| ATC class | Patients (≥65) |
|---|---|
| **SSRIs** (N06AB) | 26,838 |
| **TCAs / non-selective monoamine reuptake inhibitors** (N06AA) | 8,190 |
| **Other antidepressants** (N06AX) | 41,859 |
| MAOIs (N06AF) | 37 |

The N06AX "other" bucket is heterogeneous, so broken down by ingredient:

| Ingredient (functional class) | Patients (≥65) |
|---|---|
| Trazodone (serotonin modulator) | 18,382 |
| Mirtazapine (NaSSA) | 11,751 |
| Duloxetine (**SNRI**) | 9,271 |
| Bupropion (NDRI) | 6,975 |
| Venlafaxine (**SNRI**) | 4,380 |
| Desvenlafaxine (SNRI) | 483 |
| Vortioxetine | 480 |
| Others (vilazodone, milnacipran, nefazodone, etc.) | <200 each |

## Bottom line

By **individual class**, the most commonly used antidepressants in older adults are:

1. **SSRIs** — the single largest true class (~26,800 patients). SSRIs (e.g., sertraline, escitalopram, citalopram) are the guideline-recommended first-line choice in geriatric depression.
2. **Trazodone** — ~18,400 patients, though much of this reflects low-dose use as a sleep aid rather than for depression.
3. **Mirtazapine** — ~11,800 patients (also frequently used for sleep/appetite in frail elderly).
4. **SNRIs** (duloxetine + venlafaxine + desvenlafaxine ≈ 14,100 patients combined) — duloxetine especially, often for comorbid neuropathic/musculoskeletal pain.
5. **TCAs** (~8,200) — declining use, relevant because they are on the **Beers Criteria** as potentially inappropriate in older adults due to anticholinergic burden.

**Caveat:** counts reflect prescribing/exposure records and include off-label indications (trazodone/mirtazapine for insomnia). If you want this filtered to a depression diagnosis, or expressed as prevalence per person-year, I can refine the query.
